events.title: Proposed change: preserve app-server error details in RPC exceptions
events.body:
In `app/codex_rpc.py`, raise a dedicated RPC error that retains the response’s `error` object and formats its code, message, and data for owner-visible diagnostics. Current code serializes the object into a generic `RuntimeError`, making callers parse a string and risking loss of useful structure. Keep process and protocol defaults unchanged.
Add a deterministic test with a fake JSON-RPC response containing `error` code, message, and data. Assert the raised exception exposes the original fields and a readable message; no network or real Codex process required.
Callers may depend on catching `RuntimeError` or matching its current JSON string. Preserve `RuntimeError` compatibility, for example with a subclass. Falsified if repository callers already reliably surface the existing error string, or if tests show the structured exception breaks their handling without improving diagnostics.

events.title: Remove the RPC timeout floor
events.body:
Ji An: Change call() to compute remaining = deadline - time.monotonic(), raise TimeoutError when remaining <= 0, and otherwise pass remaining to read(). The current max(0.1, remaining) requests at least 100 ms even when less budget remains. Critic pass: this does not establish a hard wall-clock deadline. Revised claim: the change removes an intentional source of timeout overshoot. Keep live model defaults unchanged.
Use a fake monotonic clock and stub send/read; no subprocess or network. With 20 ms remaining, assert read receives 0.02 rather than 0.1. With the deadline reached, assert read is never called and TimeoutError is raised. Falsify the claim if any requested read timeout exceeds the remaining budget.
OS scheduling and parsing can still exceed the deadline. Tests were proposed, not executed. Only supplied source supports this proposal; no second lead contribution was supplied, so joint experiment selection remains pending.

events.title: Clean up the app-server when initialization fails
events.body:
Change CodexRPC.__init__ to wrap initialization and the initialized notification in try/except; on failure, close the selector and terminate and reap the child process, then re-raise the original exception. Critic: cleanup can itself fail or mask the initialization error. Revised proposal: make cleanup best-effort and preserve the original exception; keep the existing model defaults.
Use a fake process and selector, with no network or real subprocess. Force initialize to raise, then assert that cleanup was attempted, the child was reaped, and the original exception propagated.
The change is falsified as a reliability improvement if a deterministic test shows initialization failures already leave no live child or registered selector, or if cleanup masks the original error. This is one proposed experiment; the supplied outcomes require both lead seats to contribute before an experiment is chosen.

events.title: Critique: structured RPC errors are the strongest focused proposal
events.body:
The evidence supports Ji Eun’s proposal: `call()` currently turns the JSON-RPC error object into a JSON string inside a generic `RuntimeError`, so callers cannot inspect fields without parsing. Preserve compatibility with a `RuntimeError` subclass carrying the original error object and exposing code, message, and data. Ji An identifies a real timeout-floor issue, but the supplied source alone does not establish its practical impact; a 100 ms requested read can overshoot a nearly exhausted budget, while scheduling and parsing remain outside that limit. Initialization cleanup addresses a plausible child-process leak, but the proposal does not establish how often initialization fails or whether existing callers close after failure. The two recent outcomes require both lead
Decisive deterministic regression: feed `call()` a fake JSON-RPC error response with code, message, and nested data; assert the exception remains catchable as `RuntimeError`, exposes the original structured fields, and formats a readable message. This directly tests the reported information-loss claim without a network or real Codex process.
Existing callers may depend on the current serialized exception text. The subclass preserves catch compatibility, but exact string matching could still change. No implementation or tests were run.

events.title: Prioritize initialization-failure cleanup
events.body:
Ji An: Both lead proposals are now supplied. The strongest source-supported issue is that failed initialization has no cleanup path after spawning the child and registering stdout. Prefer testing that proposal first. Critic pass: wrap the initialized notification too, and cover partial setup failures. My timeout proposal removes the explicit 100 ms floor but cannot guarantee a wall-clock deadline. Ji Eun’s structured exception helps programmatic inspection; the current serialization already preserves JSON error details, so improved owner-visible diagnostics remain unproven.
Propose an offline fake-process/selector regression: inject failures during selector registration, initialize, and the initialized send. Assert cleanup attempts release acquired resources and reap the child; inject cleanup failures separately and assert the original exception survives. Include a successful-construction control. Tests have not been executed.
Best-effort cleanup cannot guarantee reaping if termination or waiting fails. Caller behavior and diagnostic presentation are unavailable in the supplied material. Keep live model defaults unchanged; Self-Refine motivates critique and revision, not evidence that these changes work.

events.title: Revised proposal: clean up failed initialization
events.body:
The constructor can leave a child process and selector open if initialization or the initialized notification fails, because callers never receive an instance to close. Wrap setup in best-effort cleanup and re-raise the original exception. Ji Eun’s structured error is plausible, but the supplied code already includes the full error object in the exception string; caller evidence is needed to show a diagnostic benefit. Ji An identifies a real intentional timeout overshoot, though removing the floor does not guarantee a hard deadline. A simpler alternative for the cleanup change is to reuse close(), provided cleanup failures cannot replace the original exception and partially initialized resources are handled.
Without a real process or network, use fake process and selector objects, force initialization to fail, and verify termination and reaping are attempted, the selector is closed, and the original exception survives even if cleanup fails. Also test failure while sending the initialized notification. Tests are proposed, not executed.
Cleanup must handle failures before selector registration and avoid masking the original error. The supplied outcomes require both lead seats to contribute before an experiment is selected; their contributions are not identified here, so selection remains pending.

events.title: Defer an isolated patch
events.body:
The supplied record offers competing hypotheses but no caller evidence or executed regression to establish which change improves diagnostics most. Structured RPC errors retain RuntimeError compatibility, but the current exception string already includes the full error object. Initialization cleanup and timeout-floor removal are plausible reliability fixes, yet their practical impact is unverified. The two recorded outcomes require both lead seats to contribute before selecting an experiment; the supplied material does not identify those contributions.
No regression is justified for selection from the supplied evidence alone. If revisited, test initialization failure cleanup with fake process and selector objects, including cleanup failures and initialized-notification failure; assert resources are released and the original exception propagates.
Choosing any proposal now would treat an unverified hypothesis as the selected experiment. No source changes or tests were run.

outcome: The panel found insufficient evidence for a code change.
